title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka
main_claim: Every complex K3 surface X satisfies CAP (so it is Oka): any holomorphic map from a neighbourhood of a compact convex K⊂C^m into X can be uniformly approximated on K by entire maps C^m→X. The proof has five parts. (1) A local one-variable enlargement property L, with passive parameters, follows from two transverse complete strips. (2) L at every point implies CAP, via a polynomial-automorphism concentration onto polydiscs and then removal of polytope faces using Hölder-trace gluing. (3) In the projective case, L comes from two Chen–Gounelas genus-one families. (4) An open set of periods is handled by exact symplectic sewing of infinite annulus chains on smoothings of a union of two quadrics. (5) For each positive integral v, a relatively open set of D_v is handled using a j=0 isotrivial elliptic center, with conservation of imaginary action. A Ratner/Borel-density orbit argument plus Torelli then covers all periods with rational rank 0, 1 or 2.

issues.description: The class-VII classification ('Oka iff Hopf or Enoki') depends on the companion manuscript's global spherical shell theorem [OpenAIGSS, Thm 1.1]. That is the GSS conjecture, which is open, and the companion's proof is not checked here. The paper says explicitly that this is not an input to the K3 theorem, so it does not affect the main result.
issues.evidence: 'When b_2>0, the global spherical shell theorem [OpenAIGSS, Theorem 1.1] therefore applies, so the surface is a Kato surface.'

issues.location: sections/degeneration.tex, final subsection 'Coverage and unrestricted deformation'; sections/rational.tex Lemma rat:strips
issues.description: Several uniformity claims are argued only briefly rather than with explicit estimates: that seam inverse branches, period adjustments, coverage and transversality all persist under deformation of the finite raw atlas, and that the action error epsilon_t stays uniform under arbitrary recentering. I traced the logic and it holds: the finite compact atlas, recentering by translations, and errors that never accumulate because each block is compared with its own model. I found no failing step, but a referee would want these written out.
issues.evidence: 'Thus all the domain, derivative, period-adjustment, coverage, and transversality estimates persist in a sufficiently small unrestricted deformation neighborhood.'

coverage:
I read every section in full: introduction, local, gluing, globalization, projective, sewing, degeneration, rational, dynamics, dense.

Checks made by hand:
- Prop loc:criterion: the fixed-point equation, the contraction constants (T(0) ≤ M²η; DT ≤ M²κ(1+κL0)η; ball radius L0 = 2M²+1), and the domain and coordinate-smallness bookkeeping on U_A and U_B.
- Lemma loc:pieces: the geometry.
- Lemma loc:splitting: the Cauchy–Green bound.
- Prop loc:planar: the spoke and sector filling.
- Cor loc:disc.
- Lemma ana:concentration / Prop ana:polydisc: the domains of F_A and F_B', the overlap identity Φ_d(s(h),ξ(h)) = h, and the order of choices.
- The induction A_{n-1} ⇒ A_n and the real-interface trace splitting.
- Sewing: the symplectic and exactness identities (u_w+v_p = -u_w v_p + u_p v_w; v_0 = -∫v u_w), the cancellation between the Hamiltonian convention X_H = (H_p, -H_w) and X_{G_j} - X_{G_{j+1}∘J}, the Fourier splitting telescoping and its decay bound uniform in chain length, and the domain-covering argument.
- Degeneration: the small resolution of xy = αt, the log-symplectic residues (K+E = 0 on both components), the regular-pencil genericity case analysis on Bl_Z Q, and the seam leading terms.
- Rational center: tr(g|H²) = 2 + χ(Fix) = -8 gives r = 2, so the invariant lattice is U; (v,gv) = -d and the plane is positive; Eichler; the fixed-locus Euler-characteristic contradiction showing the base action is trivial; the action-conservation confinement; and the two-cycle torus/class-me contradiction.
- Dynamics: the h-module decomposition so(V) = h ⊕ so(P) ⊕ W⊗P, the intermediate subalgebras, Borel-density rationality, and maximality of SO(1,19) in SO(2,19).
- The Torelli step and the three-case conclusion.

Not checked line by line: the Hörmander/elliptic interior estimates, Lemma glue:interval (Hermite jet matching), and the precise statements of the cited external theorems (Chen–Gounelas Thm A for genus 1, ForstnericCAP, Ratner).

A numeric spot-check of the concentration lemma was inconclusive: random sampling never landed in the |x_1| > r_1 region.
sibling_notes: No sibling entries existed for family 042 when I checked. Possibly relevant to other branches: the class-VII part of this paper's surface-classification corollary depends on the companion OpenAIGSS (global spherical shell) manuscript. Any branch auditing OpenAIGSS should know that its theorem is cited here only for that corollary, not for the K3 result.
